text: October consumer prices rose 0.4% and core prices (without food and energy) 0.3%, both above forecasts of 0.3% and 0.2%. No yearly rate was published because of last year's shutdown data gap.

The 2-year Treasury yield jumped more than 15 bp to about 4.70% and the 10-year rose about 7 bp to 4.94% after the report and Governor Waller's comment that a half-point December hike could be needed.
Gold fell about 1.6% to near $4,075 and silver about 2% to near $52.19 before the report, giving back part of Monday's rally after Waller's remarks.
On Monday the S&P 500 rose 2.35% and the Nasdaq 2.74%, the S&P's best day since April, while Nvidia fell about 4% on its board's review of CEO Jensen Huang.
After the inflation report, S&P 500 futures were down about 0.5% and Nasdaq-100 futures about 1.2%.
Brent settled 5.85% lower at $92.57 on Monday and slipped below $90 early Tuesday for the first time since August, as signs of restraint toward Iran grew.
Gold miners jumped on Monday: GDX closed up 4.41% at $91.46 and SLV up 2.71% at $48.14.
